title: Insurance Coverage & Claims Reimbursement Memo: Balance Share on Member Appeals to Out-of-Network Plans Paying First
content:
**Reimbursement memo — Insurance Coverage & Claims, member appeals to an out-of-network plan that pays first.**

The first-plan member appeal's balance share is the out-of-network balance assigned to the member on the coverage within the last six months divided by that balance plus the contractual adjustments on the coverage within the same six months, where such a balance exists; it is the same share taken over the last twelve months where no such balance falls within six months but one falls within twelve months; otherwise it is one. Under the first-plan member appeal, the contested charges are multiplied by the balance share.

The out-of-network balance is the patient-responsibility amount of the out-of-network balance type on the coverage; the contractual adjustments are the write-offs on the coverage in the same window.

## Worked example (hypothetical coverage)

Over the last six months the coverage shows an out-of-network balance of 75.00 USD and contractual adjustments of 225.00 USD. A balance exists within six months, so the six-month share applies: 75.00 divided by 75.00 plus 225.00, that is 300.00, giving 0.25. Contested charges of 640.00 USD multiplied by 0.25 give 160.00 USD.

Had the coverage carried no out-of-network balance in the last six months but 60.00 USD of it, against 180.00 USD of contractual adjustments, in the last twelve months, the twelve-month share would apply: 60.00 divided by 240.00, also 0.25. With no out-of-network balance in either window, the share is one and the contested charges stay at billed value.
